yield-accumulator.description: Consolidates yield strategy rewards from multiple stablecoins into a single reward token for simplified Phlimbo distribution. Part of the Phoenix/Behodler ecosystem.
yield-accumulator.notes: External claimers swap their reward token holdings for pending yield strategy rewards at a discount, enabling decentralized conversion without protocol oracles/AMMs.
yield-accumulator.knownIssuesSource: CLAUDE.md project documentation + source code NatSpec comments
knownIssues: Dual-unpause mechanism - both owner AND pauser can unpause (intentional redundancy, Behodler3 pattern)
Decimal normalization to 18 decimals internally (documented design)
Circular reference between Phlimbo and StableYieldAccumulator (documented deployment order)
No oracles/AMMs - uses assumed 1:1 exchange rates for stablecoins (owner can adjust for permanent depegs)
Owner trust assumptions for registering strategies, setting exchange rates, pausing tokens (operational risk)
Pauser trust assumptions - designated pauser can pause contract operations
External yield strategy behavior assumptions (out of scope)
Token config with zero decimals and zero exchange rate defaults to 18 decimals and 1:1 rate
designDecisions: Discount rate incentivizes external claimers to pay gas costs for conversion
Token pause mechanism for black swan events (e.g., stablecoin depeg)
Normalized exchange rates to 18 decimals for cross-token comparison
Minter address holds deposits in yield strategies; accumulator queries yield via minter

phlimbo-linear.description: PhlimboEA - Staking yield farm for phUSD tokens with Linear Depletion reward distribution
phlimbo-linear.notes: Part of the Phoenix/Behodler ecosystem. Main contract receives rewards from yield-accumulator and distributes them to stakers.
phlimbo-linear.knownIssuesSource: phoenix-phase-2 parent project (lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/known-issues.md) + source code analysis
knownIssues: Two-step APY setting process (intentional security feature) - requires two calls within 100 blocks to commit
First depositor attack mitigated via MINIMUM_STAKE (0.001 phUSD / 1e15 wei) - not a vulnerability
Dust prevention on withdrawal - withdrawing to below MINIMUM_STAKE forces full withdrawal
pauseWithdraw does NOT claim rewards or update pool (emergency exit mechanism by design)
Owner trust assumptions - centralized control for pausing, APY setting, yield accumulator configuration
Pauser trust assumptions - designated pauser can pause/unpause contract operations
PhlimboEA requires minting rights on phUSD token (configuration requirement, not bug)
Circular reference with StableYieldAccumulator - documented deployment order dependency
External yield strategy behavior assumptions (out of scope)
Zero APY operation is supported and expected (no phUSD emissions, only stable rewards)
designDecisions: Linear depletion model for reward distribution (rewardBalance / depletionDuration)
Rate recalculates after each balance change (collection or distribution)
Dual reward system: phUSD (minted based on APY) + stable tokens (from yield accumulator)
Emergency transfer pauses contract and moves all tokens to recipient

phoenix-vault.description: Yield strategy adapter contracts for integrating with external ERC4626 vaults. Includes surplus (yield) tracking and percentage-based surplus withdrawal. Concrete implementation for Tokemak AutoDOLA.
phoenix-vault.notes: Part of the Phoenix/Behodler ecosystem. Provides adapter pattern for yield-generating protocols with two-phase emergency withdrawal for rugpull protection.
knownIssues: M1 (MEDIUM): Unlimited token approvals to external contracts - AutoDolaYieldStrategy grants type(uint256).max approval to autoDOLA vault and MainRewarder. Risk if external contracts compromised.
L1 (LOW): Emergency withdrawal missing re-stake logic - _emergencyWithdraw() does not re-stake remaining shares after partial withdrawal, causing yield generation to stop for leftover shares.
L2 (LOW): No balance validation in emergency withdrawal - should check available balance before withdrawal attempt.
No On-Chain Balance Verification - SurplusWithdrawer system cannot verify client internal balance on-chain; relies on caller providing accurate clientInternalBalance parameter.
No Rate Limiting - No built-in limits on withdrawal frequency or amounts in SurplusWithdrawer.
No Recipient Whitelist - Withdrawer owner can specify any recipient address for surplus withdrawals.
No Automated Pause/Circuit Breaker - No automatic pause mechanism for anomalous withdrawal patterns.
No Time-Based Controls - No timelock or delay on surplus withdrawals (only totalWithdrawal has two-phase mechanism).
Client Internal Balance Trust - Incorrect clientInternalBalance values can result in over-withdrawal (withdrawing principal instead of just surplus).
Vault Owner Trust Assumption - Vault owner has complete control over authorized withdrawers; malicious vault owner can authorize a drainer.
Token Standard Compliance Assumption - System assumes standard ERC20 tokens without transfer hooks or reentrancy vectors.
Authorized Withdrawer Trust - Authorized withdrawers have unrestricted access to ALL client balances in the vault (no per-client restrictions).
AutoDolaYieldStrategy single-token constraint - Only supports DOLA token, not arbitrary ERC20s (architectural decision, not bug).
designDecisions: Two-phase emergency withdrawal (totalWithdrawal) with 24h waiting period and 48h execution window for rugpull protection
Percentage-based surplus withdrawal (1-100%) for treasury management flexibility
Multi-client authorization model - multiple clients can be authorized on a single vault
Authorized withdrawer pattern - separates withdrawal capability from balance ownership
Balance caching at totalWithdrawal initiation to prevent manipulation during waiting period
systemAssumptions: Caller provides accurate clientInternalBalance from client's accounting system
Vault owner acts in best interest of protocol and clients
Majority of multisig signers are honest and vigilant
Authorized withdrawer contracts are bug-free and audited
